recaps.transcript: Okay, second session with Priya. Picking up from last week, we built the exposure hierarchy for her flying fear and today she actually started at the bottom rung, which for her is just looking at flight booking sites. She did it twice this week, and she said the first time her anxiety was maybe a seven out of ten and the second time a five, so the habituation is starting, slowly. Hmm, she also said something contradictory, that she is proud of herself but also that she feels silly for needing a ladder for something other people just do. I did not push on that, I just reflected it. Sleep is unchanged, five, six hours. She mentioned her manager moved the standup to Mondays, which she hates, but she handled it, she asked for the agenda in advance. We agreed the next step is the rung above, watching takeoff videos for ten minutes a day, and she will log her ratings. I want to keep an eye on the self-critical thread, it showed up again when she called herself silly.

recaps.transcript: Third session with Mr. Ahmadi, interpreter on the phone again, the agency one, and the connection was patchy, we lost maybe two minutes in the middle. He is still grieving his brother, it has been eight months, and he says two things that sit side by side: he wants to stop talking about him every week, and also he cannot imagine a session where they do not. I did not try to resolve that, we just sat with both. He brought the prayer beads his brother gave him and held them the whole hour. He said in his home country people visited for forty days, here nobody came after the funeral, and that is the loneliness that keeps coming back. When I reflected that, he cried, quietly, and then apologised for crying, which we have talked about before. He said hearing his own language through the interpreter made it feel less like a translation. Small thing, he ate dinner with his wife twice this week, first time since the funeral. Next week we continue with the beads if he wants, and I want to ask more about the forty days and what they meant to him.

recaps.transcript: Fourth session with Elena, couples work but she came alone, partner away for work. She said the argument on Saturday started over the dishwasher and ended with him sleeping in the spare room, which is the third time this month. Then, and this is where I slowed down, she said she sometimes wonders what the point is, and when I asked directly about self-harm or suicide she said no, no thoughts like that, it was about the marriage, not her life. Good, that is documented. She said the worst part is that he goes cold and she chases, and she knows she chases, and she cannot stop. I named the cycle, pursuer and withdrawer, and she recognised it instantly, said it was her parents' dance too. She asked me whether I think they can survive, and I did not answer yes or no, I said that is what the work is for. Homework, she will write down what she actually wanted to say under the anger, one incident. Next time both of them come in and we do the same exercise live. recaps.transcript: Session six with Tomas, EMDR prep continuing. We did the window of tolerance mapping again and this time he could name the early signs without me prompting, jaw, shoulders, the feeling like the room gets smaller. Then, mid-sentence about his father, he stopped and said he was out of the window, so we grounded, feet on the floor, named five things in the room, and he came back in about four minutes, which is faster than last month. He said the memory was there but further away, like through a window, his words. No reprocessing today, I held the frame, resourcing only. He asked when we start the actual EMDR, and I said when his window holds for a full session, and he took that well, he said he would rather be bored than flooded. Childhood history, the shouting, the belt, he referenced it without going in. He slept badly, three nights of five or six hours. Plan is bilateral stimulation with the calm place again next week, then reassess. I want to track the jaw cue as an early marker and see if it moves earlier each session.

recaps.transcript: Fifth session with Rosa, interpreter joined, the same one as before, which helps. She had a scan on Monday, abdominal, and the results are not back yet, so the whole session was about the wait. She told me she checked the patient portal eleven times on Monday, she counted, and by Tuesday she made a deal with herself, twice in the morning, twice at night, which she kept. Picking up from last week, we mapped the morning routine again and it turns out the shouting starts at the sock stage, every single day, socks. Dad laughed, then said it is not funny, and he is right. The seven-year-old has started calling himself stupid when he cannot find things, which stopped the room, and mum said she has heard it too, so that is the thing we are working on now. We tried the two-choice rule, socks are this pair or that pair, nothing else, and they will run it for a week and text me how it goes. There is also a real question about whether the school mornings are just too tight, both parents leave at eight, so we are going to look at bedtime moving twenty minutes earlier. They disagree about whether the younger one is just strong-willed or actually struggling, and I did not resolve it, we will keep it open. Next week the kids come for the first time, so I will do the session in two parts, parents first, then play with the little one while mum and dad watch.

recaps.transcript: Session seven with Nino. She said something at the start that reframed the whole hour, that she feels like two people, the one who is proud of leaving and the one who is ashamed of leaving, and she is tired of pretending the proud one is the real one. I did not interpret it, I just stayed with it, and she sat with the silence better than she has before, nearly a full minute. Her English is good but when it gets emotional she reaches for her first language, she said three words in Georgian today and then translated them for me, roughly, something like without the ground. So that became the image for the hour. Work is fine, she got the contract extension. She saw her mother's name pop up on her phone and did not answer, third time, and she noticed the relief, and then the guilt about the relief. No rush from me on any of it. Next week I will bring back the image of no ground and ask where she learned to stand without it. I am tracking whether the shame side gets more airtime than the pride side, because she leads with pride and hides the rest.

Sleep diary came back and it is not as bad as she feared, she averages five and a half hours but the wake after sleep onset is the problem, about ninety minutes most nights. recaps.transcript: Session two with Hannah, picking up from the intake. She came in with a list, actual paper list, reasons to leave and reasons to stay, and the lists are almost the same length, which is the whole problem, she said. recaps.transcript: Session eleven with Pavel, GAD, cognitive work continuing. He brought the thought record, four entries, and the one that mattered was the one about the team meeting, where he wrote that everyone would notice his hands shaking and conclude he is not ready for the lead role. We tested it together, evidence for, evidence against, and the against column won on the facts, three people have actually told him he is ready, one of them his director. Plan, he will do the decatastrophising sheet for the next meeting, and we will review it before it happens, not after. Next focus, the safety behaviours in meetings, he sits at the back near the door and always pre-reads the agenda twice, and I want to map what those buy him.

recaps.transcript: Session thirteen with Nadia, anger work, and this one had a moment. She was describing the fight with her sister, the inheritance one, and she said she could have killed her, meaning it as a figure of speech, and I asked directly, because that is what you do, whether she had thoughts of harming her sister or anyone, and she said no, of course not, it is a saying, and she was not offended, she said she would rather I ask. So that is documented. The real material is the shame under the anger, she apologises to furniture, her line, and we tracked it to the scene at her mother's funeral where she was told to stop crying because it was upsetting the guests. She has been swallowing ever since, her word again, she is full of lines today. She walked the long way home to avoid her sister's street, and she knows it, and she does not want to stop doing it yet, which we respected. Plan, she writes the unsent letter to the aunt who said the funeral thing. Next week, the swallowing, and whether it connects to the jaw tension she reported at intake.

recaps.transcript: Session ten with Grace, no, the other Grace, I need to start using surnames in these, Graham. Grace Graham, health anxiety, and the thyroid thing is still the engine. She is on levothyroxine, seventy-five micrograms, has been for a year, and the endocrinologist says the numbers are fine, and she believes the numbers and not the endocrinologist, if that makes sense, she said it better than that. We did the formulation today, the maintenance cycle, how the checking keeps the worry alive, she checks her neck in every reflective surface, shop windows, phone screen, and she counted, forty times a day, which shocked her. So the behavioural experiment is the phone screen one, she photographs the neck once a day, one photo, and no mirrors in between, and she will rate the anxiety before and after checking. She is terrified the ratings will go up, and I said they might, at first, and that is data too. Sleep is six hours. She asked whether I think she is making it up, and I said no, the worry is real, the thyroid is real, they can both be real. Next week the photo experiment review, and I want to ask what she thinks the checking buys her, protection from what exactly.

recaps.transcript: Session four with Kacper, and we are doing the dream work, which is new for me with him, he brought one unprompted. Picking up from last week, he said the falling dream has changed, before it was falling off a roof, and now it is falling off a scaffold, which he says is different because a scaffold is something you build, his observation, I did not supply it. He writes them in Polish, the dreams, then translates in the room, and he says the translation loses the texture, and we agreed he can read the Polish aloud first and then tell me, which he did, and it sounded different, slower, more like a confession. Work is the scaffold, he is on a contract that ends in March, and he is scaffolding someone else's project, again his words, I am noticing he is very good at images. Sleep is five hours, he wakes at four, the falling happens in the last hour before waking. He is not drinking, he said that unprompted too, three months dry. Plan, he keeps the dream diary, one line per dream, no analysis, and reads the next one in Polish first. Next week I want the scaffold, what he is building and who for, and I will not interpret the falling before he does.

recaps.transcript: Second session with Linh, interpreter on video, Vietnamese, and this week the internet held, last week it did not, so we got a full hour, which is its own win. Picking up from last week, the class thing, she teaches, no, she is a teaching assistant, and the observation lesson is in two weeks and she has been rehearsing answers to questions nobody has asked yet, in the shower, on the bus. We named the fortune telling, she does not like the term, so we call it the rehearsal, her term, and the experiment is to rehearse once, deliberately, and then stop and note what actually happens, and I asked her to note the gap between the rehearsal and the reality. She said something quietly, through the interpreter, that her mother in Da Nang thinks she is doing so well and she cannot tell her about the anxiety, because the sacrifice would look wasted, roughly, the interpreter and I both sat with that one. She avoids the staff room, eats at her desk. Sleep is okay. She agreed to one staff room coffee this week, ten minutes, timer on. Next week, the mother material, if it comes, and the coffee debrief. I want to be careful not to turn the coffee into a test.
